rules.statement: Asymmetric key abstractions must expose public key material as SubjectPublicKeyInfo (SPKI) DER, not as a System.Security.Cryptography.AsymmetricAlgorithm instance.
rules.why: .NET post-quantum types (MLDsa, SlhDsa, MLKem, CompositeMLDsa) and Edwards-curve OKP keys do not derive from AsymmetricAlgorithm. DER key material is the only surface they share with RSA/ECC, so a model built around AsymmetricAlgorithm cannot represent them.
rules.check: Look for asymmetric key base types or interfaces that return or accept AsymmetricAlgorithm as the general public-key representation, such as an ExportAsymmetricAlgorithm() member, instead of an SPKI DER export. Family-specific accessors like ExportRSA()/ExportECDsa() are fine.

rules.statement: Put cryptographic operations (sign/verify, encapsulate/decapsulate) on algorithm-specific abstractions, never on the shared asymmetric key base type.
rules.why: The operations differ by algorithm family and do not generalize. This matches Microsoft's choice not to give the PQC types a common base class.
rules.check: Look for SignData/VerifyData/Encapsulate/Decapsulate-style members added to a common asymmetric key base class or interface instead of an algorithm-specific type.

rules.statement: Key-material export methods must write into a caller-supplied generic buffer writer (`void Export...<TWriter>(ref TWriter destination) where TWriter : IBufferWriter<byte>, allows ref struct`) instead of returning a byte[].
rules.why: This follows the general buffer convention: it avoids array allocations and lets the caller choose the backing storage.
rules.check: Look for new or changed export/encode methods for key or DER material that return byte[] instead of writing to a ref TWriter constrained to IBufferWriter<byte> with allows ref struct.

rules.statement: Use a non-sensitive pooled buffer writer (`BufferFactory.CreatePooledBufferWriter(isSensitive: false)`, backed by the shared MemoryPool) for public, non-secret material such as SPKI public keys, and keep the pinned SecureMemoryPool for secret material.
rules.why: The public half of a key is not secret, so it does not need the more expensive pinned secure pool.
rules.check: Look for public-key or other non-secret encoding that rents a sensitive or secure buffer. Also flag private-key material written to a non-sensitive pooled writer.
